attack_1_fake_missing.detail: JEV_SELFTEST_FAKE_MISSING appends a nonexistent path to the suite list; the loop's genuine `[ ! -x ]` branch fires on a genuinely-absent path (rc=1, ABSENT named). Only list membership is artificial; the exercised branch, message, and exit are the real missing-suite path (fresh clone, partial checkout). Ran live: --selftest OK. The -x test conflates missing with non-executable, but the message ('not executable on disk') covers both honestly.

attack_2_runtime.detail: Measured 5.05s live (3/3 PASS). gates.sh was ~11s for 10-70, so 80 adds ~45% — the slowest stage. Worth it, marginally: these three suites guard the lane's newest instruments (the exact class that rotted: unverified gates), and nothing else runs them automatically (tick runs lane-status.sh only; the suites are hand-runnable but hand-unrun). Verdict conditional: keep while total gates.sh stays under ~30s; past that, split 80 out of the default run rather than deleting coverage. The hardcoded '3 suites PASS' message will stale on a 4th suite — cosmetic, noted.

attack_3_exclusions.verify_other_reasons_itself: JUSTIFIED BUT MOST PROCEDURAL: live STATUS+sidecar reads are technically no worse than gate 70's live TESTS.md reads, so the stated reason (separate decision pending per ruling) is deference rather than mechanics. Acceptable — but it needs its own re-examination condition (promote when sidecar coverage holds stable across N commits), or this exclusion becomes permanent caution. Recommended, not demanded.
